text: # onmywave.fm macOS app requirements
Current requirements, 17 October 2026. User behavior and acceptance scenarios are defined in [the radio experience PRD](docs/RADIO_EXPERIENCE.md).

Build a separate macOS music player for a listener’s existing Jellyfin library, with optional personal radio hosting. Music works without AI setup. A separately enabled local workflow collects selected news sources, assesses new stories, and saves short recordings. A separately enabled DJ plays eligible saved recordings at suitable song endings. Both switches default off. Mood-based music selection remains future work.
## Product scope

The app is a new project in `desktop-light/`, separate from the existing Feishin desktop fork in `desktop/`. Use the existing app as a reference for Jellyfin integration, metadata presentation, library browsing, and playlist behavior. Build the new app with the stack defined below.

Support macOS and Jellyfin only in the first version. Jellyfin remains the source of music files, library metadata, access permissions, and server playlists. The new app does not require uploading or importing another copy of the music collection.
The interface should expose the agreed functions directly, with sensible defaults and few customization settings.

On macOS, the red close control and Close Window (⌘W) hide the window while the app keeps running. Keep the same music session, current page, unsaved drafts and pending operations in memory. Closing does not save edits, authorize or retry preparation, or cancel previously authorized work. Activating the app shows the same window and restores it if minimized. Quit (⌘Q) stops playback and preparation through the existing shutdown path and discards unsaved drafts. Launching again restores the saved music session paused.
## Visual design

Use Apple Music and Yandex Music as visual references for a light, simple macOS interface. Aim for a contemporary 2026 feel with more generous whitespace, softer rounded forms, light controls, and a continuous composition. Keep onmywave.fm's own identity. Avoid chopping the interface into dense rectangular panels.
### Color direction
- Use the soft off-white main background `#fbfbfc`.
- Use pale neutral gray for the sidebar `#f0f0f3`, secondary panels `#f7f7f9`, and subtle separators `#e6e6ea`.
- Use near-black primary text `#202024` and muted secondary text `#626674`.
- Use the rose-red primary accent `#c92843` consistently for selected navigation, primary actions, active controls and focus. Use `#b5223a` for primary hover and `#fbecef` for soft accent surfaces.
- Keep large surfaces neutral so album artwork provides most of the color.
- Disabled controls use neutral surfaces and readable muted text. These values record the implemented light palette; verify any future adjustment against the same contrast and state requirements.
### Layout and controls
- Use a compact sidebar with the agreed music and news categories and a spacious main content area.
- Present songs in a clean table and albums in an artwork grid.
- Keep the player persistent as an inset floating rounded surface, with circular transport controls and enough spacing to distinguish each action. Make secondary playback options available on demand.

- Use generous padding and row spacing, clear typography, softly rounded window corners and artwork, pill-shaped search and filter controls, and rounded selection states. Prefer whitespace and subtle surface changes to hard borders.

- Follow familiar macOS window and interaction conventions, including keyboard navigation and visible focus states. Command-F focuses the current music search. Additional modifiers and Control-F retain their native behavior instead of redirecting focus to library search.
- Keep common actions easy to find. Reveal secondary actions through row menus or contextual controls.
- Give news profile setup and DJs simple forms with clear labels.
- Use restrained motion and respect reduced-motion preferences.
### Typography and spacing

Use [Manrope from Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Manrope) at weight 600 for the wordmark and headings, and [Inter from Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Inter) at weights 400 and 500 for interface text. Keep the macOS system font for native operating-system chrome. Bundle the chosen app fonts rather than requiring a runtime network request.
Use these initial design targets in logical points, adjusting only where actual font metrics and window resizing require it:
| Element | Target |
| Page title | 28 pt, weight 600 |
| Song title and navigation | 14 pt with 20 pt line height |
| Secondary artist text | 12 pt with 18 pt line height |
| Column headers | 11 pt with 16 pt line height |
| Metadata values | 13 pt with 20 pt line height |
| Spacing scale | Multiples of 8 pt, with 4 pt optical adjustments |
| Main content padding | 24 to 32 pt |
| Control gaps | 12 to 16 pt |
| Sidebar width | Approximately 208 pt |
| Song rows | Approximately 52 pt high |
| Row artwork | 36 pt with 8 pt corner radius |
| Search and filter controls | 32 to 36 pt high |
| Floating player | Approximately 72 pt high |

Align text baselines, table columns, icons, control centers, and outer insets consistently. Keep icon stroke weights consistent, reserve adequate hit areas, and show hover, focus, pressed, selected, and disabled states. Holding an enabled button with the pointer or Space gives immediate pressed feedback while retaining its selected colors and keyboard focus. Release restores its resting position; disabled controls remain inactive and still. Avoid animating this pressed feedback. Long titles must truncate or wrap deliberately without moving adjacent controls. Keep compact music rows, tiles, queue and player labels bounded. Collection headings use a two-line title so Play, Queue and Add remain visible; when that title is clipped, offer a keyboard-accessible Show full title disclosure after the actions. Full inspector metadata, tags, story references, source labels and preparation notes wrap within their reading surface, including text without spaces. Long account names also wrap within the connection panel, keeping library choices and recovery actions reachable without horizontal scrolling. Saved DJ names, preview labels and recovery messages must also handle long text without spaces while keeping actions reachable.
### macOS presentation

Use normal macOS window proportions, traffic lights, titlebar behavior, window shadow, and system integration. Keep content legible over a translucent sidebar or playback surface. Screenshots and design reviews should show the app in desktop context with wallpaper, menu bar, and Dock, rather than only an isolated concept board.

Keep the app airy at realistic desktop text sizes. Verify spacing and typography using the actual bundled fonts at standard and Retina display scales. Check minimum window size, resized layouts, and long metadata so production screenshots reflect an implemented layout rather than generated-image approximations.
### Design acceptance

The first version must feel light and simple across library pages, playlists, forms, and playback. Use readable text and sufficient contrast, including selected, disabled, hover, and focus states. Keep disabled labels and pending form values legible with muted text and neutral control surfaces; do not fade entire forms or primary-action labels. Disabled controls retain native disabled behavior and a distinct appearance. Keep timing labels readable in the active transition stage as well as inactive stages. Current acceptance uses windows of at least 1280×720 at normal 100% app zoom. Anton deferred smaller-window and enlarged-zoom checks, including 200%, on 16 October 2026. Retain existing responsive behavior for later verification; do not add or repeat those deferred checks in this goal. Preserve essential controls and readable content at the current baseline. Keep volume from collapsing, make sidebar navigation scrollable in short windows, and retain access to setup Save. Existing smaller-window behavior is retained for later acceptance: at narrow widths, queue/details replace the main area above the player; covered page/notice controls must not remain keyboard-focusable, and closing the drawer restores them.

A setup save must keep its pending state and any failure feedback across page navigation. Keep music navigation available, prevent overlapping setup/profile writes, retain failed drafts for explicit retry, and reject a save whose intended profile is no longer active. General DJ playback and transition edits also retain their unsaved values, pending save and errors across music pages and Settings sections. These non-secret preferences apply to this app on this Mac, so their transient drafts and active writes also survive music-account changes; quitting discards unsaved drafts. Each form saves only on explicit submission, keeps failures retryable, and blocks duplicate submissions without blocking the other form or music. General playback saves change only cadence, seeking behavior and voice volume; player profile/enable changes preserve those preferences. Merge each explicit field patch against the latest queued local state so a delayed settings save cannot reverse a newer DJ-off choice or profile selection. After a confirmed save, keep the saved values visible if the status refresh fails. Show the refresh failure with read-only Retry; do not repeat the save or clear a copied or switched profile back to an older display. Older responses must not replace newer confirmed state.

Keyboard focus must remain visible. Opening an album or playlist from its focused tile starts the detail view at the top and focuses its Back control immediately, including while reads are loading or failed. Later data updates do not replay that focus move. Returning through sidebar navigation keeps its existing focus and saved detail scroll. A focused playlist Back returns to that exact playlist tile and reveals it, or to the list heading if the tile is unavailable. When removing a queue occurrence whose Remove button owns focus, move to the next visible Remove action, then the previous visible one, or Close queue if none remain. Skip collapsed Earlier history and reveal only the needed distance above the player; removing a repeated song must remove only that occurrence. Leave focus elsewhere untouched. In All songs, albums and playlists, keep the focused song row and its checkbox, artwork, title and actions clear of the sticky heading, selection toolbar, player and changing playback notices. Arrow navigation follows each key press, including quick repeats. Reveal only the needed distance; pointer selection and passive updates must not scroll the list or take focus from a dialog or menu. Keyboard focus must leave filter popups and song action menus naturally with Tab, return after dialogs, and return to the relevant setup control after managing sources, DJs, or provider keys without losing the draft. Opening a playlist name, source name, or new listening-room name form puts focus in its name field so typing works immediately. The Add to playlist form initially focuses the new-playlist name, and choosing Create a new playlist again focuses its newly shown name field. Editing values, changing source type, or background refreshes must not move focus back. Help and confirmation dialogs start on a safe non-destructive target. Escape, Cancel, Close and backdrop dismissal return focus to the opening control when it remains available. If a dialog removes its opening control, focus the current page heading. Keep long dialog titles compact so Close and keyboard actions remain reachable at the current acceptance baseline. Preserve the full accessible title. For DJ and source deletion, show the complete target name in wrapping body text so similarly named items remain distinguishable before confirmation. Give related source checkboxes a group name and keep interactive recovery controls outside live status/error announcements.

An explicitly activated read-error retry keeps its action and error explanation visible even when the query resets to Loading. Show Retrying and an accessible busy state, keep keyboard focus, ignore repeat activation, and keep unrelated recovery actions usable. Failure restores Try again. After success, move focus to that screen’s relevant result, control or heading only if the same retry still owns focus. Tab, pointer activity, navigation, resource changes, a new overlay or window hiding cancel this focus handoff while the read continues. A retry inside a dialog or popover stays within that same still-open overlay. Initial loads and unfocused background refreshes do not move focus. If an automatic read starts while its existing Try again action still owns focus, retain that same action and explanation with Checking and an accessible busy state. Failure restores Try again. Settled success may repair focus to the same screen’s relevant visible result, control or heading when removing that focused action, subject to the same owner, user-navigation, window and overlay guards. An unrelated or disabled target must not receive focus; a relevant heading or back/count anchor can remain available while a sibling read still fails. A compound playlist refresh stays busy through both its detail and playlist-list reads; a failure in either keeps an actionable retry. Changing the search or resource leaves the obsolete retry behind and keeps the new resource's retry usable. Retry starts only the stated read operation and cannot submit a form. Existing page-specific focus handoffs still apply when recovery removes an error.
A dark theme, elaborate animations, decorative gradients, and extensive appearance customization are outside the initial design scope.
### Interface concept

Concept v4 presents the All songs view as an app window on a macOS desktop, including wallpaper, system menu bar, Dock, and native window controls. The app retains the light palette, rounded controls, airy library rows, open metadata area, and floating player. The image is a generated visual target with illustrative music data; the actual application will implement and verify the font and layout specifications below.
![macOS desktop presentation concept v4](docs/design/macos-production-concept-v4.png)
### Pinterest inspiration
- [Airy desktop player reference](https://in.pinterest.com/pin/208010077668840252/) inspires the large artwork, generous spacing, and quiet track list.

- [Apple Music dashboard concept](https://kr.pinterest.com/pin/515732594846289618/) inspires the rounded application shell, small filter pills, and separate playback surface. Use those layout ideas with our light palette.
- [Music UI desktop design by Khandaker Rasel](https://in.pinterest.com/pin/644788871650256226/) offers a reference for artwork hierarchy and a quiet library sidebar.

These are visual references rather than current Apple product specifications. Use gentle translucency only where it keeps content readable, especially the sidebar and player. Apply the same spacing, corner shapes, and control treatment to every app page.
## Project folder and stack

The new app lives in `desktop-light/` at the workspace root, alongside the existing `desktop/` and `ios/` projects. Treat `desktop-light/` as the implementation destination for these requirements. Keep the existing desktop app available as a reference.
| Component | Choice and responsibility |
| Desktop runtime | Electron for the macOS app window and native integration |
| Development and build | Vite |
| Server data | TanStack Query for library queries, caching, loading and error states, and playlist mutations |
| Music server | The existing Jellyfin server for authentication, music catalog, artwork, streaming, and playlists |

Use the existing Jellyfin server directly as the music backend. The first version does not require a new music server or a separate custom backend service. Keep local player state, selection state, and editable form drafts separate from cached server data.

Keep Electron native capabilities behind a narrow preload interface, with context isolation and renderer Node integration disabled. Store authentication secrets through operating-system protected storage. Playlist mutations must refresh or update affected cached data and clearly report failed saves.
The workspace requirements copy is `desktop-light/REQUIREMENTS.md`. The approved visual direction is the macOS desktop concept v4, saved under `desktop-light/docs/design/`.
## Navigation

Open on All songs. Provide All songs, Albums, Playlists, and News bucket, with Settings separately accessible. News bucket is the Listening Room destination for saved news and radio setup. Shared source and DJ management belong in Settings. Keep the player, DJ controls, and expandable queue available across pages.
Search and metadata filters belong within library pages. A separate full music discovery homepage is not required.
## Jellyfin connection

Connect and Save libraries retain their current focused action while submitting and after failure. Submitting a valid sign-in from a field focuses Connect before the fields lock. Block repeated submissions synchronously, retain failed inputs/checkbox choices, and keep the error and focused retry action visible at the desktop baseline. Successful library updates in Settings keep the chooser mounted for the same account and retain the focused clean save only until blur. Later Tab or navigation wins over completion feedback.

Successful sign-in hands focus from its own Connect action to the visible Choose your libraries heading, including for a different account and while library discovery is loading or empty. Saving initial library selection hands focus from its own Save action to All songs after the accepted connection update. Capture ownership before each request; later Tab, pointer activity, overlays, window hiding or another focus target cancel that handoff. Failure retains the source action. Only the current account and exact accepted library selection qualify; a stale or no-op completion cannot focus a replacement screen. Do not wait for library or audio reads to reclaim focus later.

- Accept a server address and authenticate the listener. Initial library selection always offers Use another account or server, including while discovery is loading, empty or failed. Open a sign-in form with the current server filled and username/password cleared; preserve library checkbox choices for Back. Failed authentication retains the current account. Replace it only after successful authentication, refresh available libraries and return to selection even for the same account. Successful authentication resets the checkbox draft and requires a fresh explicit library choice; only Back or a failed sign-in retains earlier checkbox edits. Back returns keyboard focus to the account-switch action.

- Let the listener select the music libraries accessible to their account. Count and submit only libraries in the current accessible list. If a prior selection becomes unavailable, explain it and let the listener explicitly save an available replacement. When no music libraries are available, offer keyboard-accessible Try again after access changes, keep the selected count at zero and prevent an empty save. An empty-list retry keeps its focused button visible as Checking libraries while pending. Repeated activation cannot restart an empty or failed list request. When libraries return, move focus from the retry action to the first available checkbox without changing selections. If access remains empty or fails, keep the retry action reachable. Leave focus alone if the listener moves elsewhere while the request is pending. Apply this recovery in initial library selection and General settings.

- Remember the connection securely across launches. Signing into another installation of this app must not invalidate this one. Use one independently generated identity for each local installation across API, artwork, direct and converted audio, and keep it across account changes, sign-out and restart. If local identity storage cannot be used, keep listening available with a temporary identity, explain that the connection may need sign-in after quitting, and do not save a new session as restorable. Keep a readable older account available until a replacement can safely clear its saved credentials. An older pending sign-in cannot replace a newer account, override recovery or undo sign-out. Confirming sign-out supersedes pending sign-ins immediately, before asynchronous preparation-pause or credential writes. If sign-out later fails, keep the originally committed account; the older pending sign-in remains superseded. A failed newer sign-in keeps the previously committed account while superseding older pending attempts. Persist connection changes in order so an older credential write cannot undo a later change or deletion. Persist the exact accepted account/library snapshot. Keep a replacement pending until its saved or explicitly session-only connection commits. Sign-out invalidates an uncommitted replacement before saving the preparation pause, so neither its credential nor its account can become active afterward. A replacement committed before sign-out becomes the account being signed out. A failed save restores the latest successfully committed account and choices only if that failed change is still current, and cannot cancel a newer pending sign-in. When an accepted account is session-only because protected storage or its persistent local identity is unavailable, remove any older restorable account record; restarting must require sign-in rather than reopen that older account. Do not overlap library saves with another library submission, account switching, sign-in or sign-out. Keep the submitted checkbox choices and Saving indicator across ordinary music navigation. A failed save keeps its choices and error after returning, allowing an explicit Save libraries retry; editing clears the prior error without saving. Successful authentication resets those drafts and errors and fetches current access, including for the same account. If expiry opens sign-in during a save, explain the wait and enable sign-in after it settles. A library save completing successfully must not dismiss the expired-session screen. Late results from an old account/authentication screen must not reopen that session; a valid Settings save must still update the collection after ordinary music navigation.

- Load catalog information and artwork from Jellyfin. Concurrent sort/filter reads for an unchanged selection must not report that the library changed merely because another view was read or cached results were evicted. Changing the actual account or selected libraries still rejects obsolete reads; a later explicit refresh reads the server again. Refresh library updates current songs and genre/tag choices, and marks cached song details, album views and playlists for a fresh read when used. Keep search, filters, selection and the listening queue during refresh. Keep the Refresh action focused while it is busy and after success or failure, unless the listener moves elsewhere. Show busy feedback, ignore repeat activation until the refresh settles, and allow Tab to continue normally. Show read failures with Retry while retaining available data. An open album reads its current title, artist, year and artwork by ID, even if it has no tracks; a metadata-only failure must leave available tracks playable. Use Jellyfin’s image revision tags for current artwork, including a song’s album-art fallback. Refreshing the collection never prepares news or enables radio.
- Respect account permissions for every read and playlist change.

- Distinguish an unreachable server, expired authentication, an empty library, and a failed operation. Offer an appropriate retry or sign-in action. Keep each Jellyfin JSON request within a 20-second deadline through the complete response body, so slow sign-in and library loads return to usable controls. A failed sign-in can be retried without suggesting a playlist change was saved. If a playlist creation loses its JSON confirmation, retain uncertain-change recovery without replay. Successful status-only playlist changes are confirmed by their response status, even if an unused body stalls. Music streaming uses its separate playback recovery.
- Keep credentials and authentication tokens out of logs.
## All songs

- Show all songs in the selected music libraries. A song or album shared by overlapping libraries appears once. Counts describe unique items, and page boundaries preserve the displayed order. Refresh library rereads current server contents.
- Search by song title, artist, and album.
- Sort the list and filter by available metadata, including genre and tags.
- Select one song or multiple songs.
- Play a song or the selected songs, add them to the queue, or add them to a playlist. Bulk actions preserve the displayed row order, regardless of selection click order.
- Display useful columns such as title, artist, album, and duration.
- Open a details panel for additional metadata.
- Keep browsing responsive for the listener's actual library size.

Metadata includes artwork, title, artist, album artist, album, duration, year, genre, tags, track number, and other fields available from Jellyfin. Missing fields must not prevent browsing or playback. Music tables and the queue identify unavailable durations explicitly. Use Untitled and Unknown artist when those details are absent. When the catalog duration is missing or invalid, use a finite positive duration reported by the current audio resource, including the offset of a converted stream. Conversion must begin at the requested song position, including when the source is already MP3. Keep this fallback local to that queue occurrence; preserve valid catalog durations and do not rewrite Jellyfin metadata. Until a finite total is available, show advancing elapsed time and an unavailable total, with seeking disabled. Apply the same availability to system seek actions while keeping Play/Pause and song changes available. Metadata display and filtering are included. Editing tags, metadata, and artwork is outside this version.
## Albums
- Browse albums with their artwork, title, and artist.

- Search albums by title or album artist within the selected libraries. Combine overlapping matches once and keep paging and ordering consistent. Open an album to see its metadata and ordered track list.
- Play an album, add its tracks to the queue, or add all its tracks to a playlist.

- Allow selecting individual tracks within an album. Keep that selection while the same album stays open through music, news or Settings navigation. Back closes the album, clears its track selection and returns keyboard focus to its tile, including after a page detour. Opening an album from the list starts a fresh selection. Library/account changes and app restart clear this temporary selection; it is not part of the saved listening queue.
## Playlists
- Show the connected account's accessible playlists.

- Create a playlist, rename an editable playlist, and open its track list. While saving, keep the name readable and keyboard focus within the dialog; repeated Save, Cancel, Close or Escape cannot repeat or interrupt the pending change. A confirmed creation opens its detail and focuses Back to playlists when the dialog still owns the interaction. Internal Tab movement keeps that ownership; an outside action, overlay or background window cancels the handoff. Definite failure keeps the draft editable after readback. An uncertain result locks Save and offers checking refreshed playlists. Rename and ordinary cancellation restore their opener.
- Add one song, multiple selected songs, or all tracks from an album.

- During an add operation, choose an existing playlist or create a new one. Keep the chosen destination, name and skip-existing option readable and keyboard-focusable while saving, with edits locked. Show unavailable Save, Cancel, Close and Review actions; repeated activation cannot duplicate the write or leave during its readback. A definite failure retains the draft for an explicit retry. An uncertain result locks changes and offers checking the refreshed playlists. Success closes the dialog and restores its opener.

- Remove tracks from editable playlists and reorder them. When a keyboard removal deletes the focused occurrence, move focus to the next surviving occurrence from the reviewed order, then the previous one, or Back if none remain. A failed removal keeps its surviving action; an uncertain removal whose row disappeared can focus the visible recovery action without claiming success. Later Tab, pointer, navigation, overlay or window changes cancel this delayed handoff.

- Each repeated song position is independently selectable and remains in the intended order when playing or queueing a playlist or selection. If Jellyfin returns missing, invalid, or reused entry identifiers, explain why Move and Remove are unavailable for those positions while keeping listening, selection, additions, renaming, and safely identified entries usable. Recheck current entries before an entry mutation; reject an absent or ambiguous target before reserving or dispatching. Never replace the whole playlist to guess which occurrence was meant. When the fetched entries change, clear selections that cannot be matched reliably; preserve uniquely identified selections. This fallback does not establish support for editing an ambiguous occurrence on a server without a safe occurrence API.
- Play a playlist or selected tracks within it.
- Save playlist changes to Jellyfin so other clients can access them.

- Explain permission restrictions and report failed saves accurately. Confirmed read-only permission disables editing; when the permission lookup is unavailable, explain that permission is unknown and let Jellyfin authorize each edit attempt. Missing, malformed or non-boolean permission data does not establish read-only access. Failure of this optional lookup must not hide otherwise available tracks. Expired authentication, an account change, or a failed metadata/track read still surfaces its own error. A denied edit remains visible without an automatic retry.

- If Jellyfin may have saved a change but the response is lost or invalid, prevent resubmission in that dialog, refresh the playlist data, and provide Close and check playlists. Never automatically repeat an uncertain creation or addition. For inline reorder or removal, keep editing unavailable until the playlist refresh succeeds and the user acknowledges checking the saved order. Keep the affected playlist’s pending state, failure and review requirement across page changes, playlist switches, library-selection saves and same-account sign-in. Other playlists and music navigation remain available. Before dispatching creation, addition, reorder or removal, durably save an account-specific recovery intent. For an addition, finish duplicate checking first and reserve only if songs remain, retaining one intent across every write batch. A failed read or empty selection must not leave a false uncertain-write lock. An unresolved creation requires a fresh complete playlist-list read and explicit acknowledgement before another creation, including creation from selected songs. Keep existing playlists usable unless their own edit is unresolved. Mark affected known playlists Review needed in the list and disable affected Add to playlist destinations, so recovery is discoverable after restart. When an Add destination is unavailable for recovery, explain why and offer Review playlists directly in the Add dialog. Creation recovery does not claim which playlist was created when Jellyfin did not return its ID. If the app quits or the outcome is uncertain, reopening still requires a fresh playlist read and explicit acknowledgement; never replay the mutation. A read begun while the write was pending cannot authorize acknowledgement. Guard rename and additions against the affected lock as well. If recovery storage is unavailable, reject edits before dispatch and keep listening available. Signing out or changing account hides the prior account’s feedback; returning to that account still requires review of its unresolved change. A late old-account result must not refresh or alter the new account.

- Playlist recovery Refresh and confirmation keep their focused control while pending, distinguish which action is running, and reject repeated or overlapping activation. Their pending lock survives music navigation. A failed confirmation retains its action when the reviewed version is still current; a later read requires confirming that newly reviewed version. Successful confirmation moves focus to the list result or detail Back only while the originating interaction still owns focus. Never acknowledge a newer recovery state using an older action.
- Handle duplicate additions consistently, with an option to skip tracks already present.
Playlist deletion, sharing, and smart playlist editing are not part of the agreed first version.
## Playback

Music Retry keeps a stable focused action through preparation and after failure. A successful retry moves focus to the persistent transport only while that exact queue occurrence and request still own the interaction. Later keyboard/pointer navigation, overlays, other music commands or a hidden window cancel the handoff. Retry of a failed saved-session read restores the queue paused and focuses Play when its own restored selection is ready. Adding other music supersedes a pending restore so it cannot hide the new selection's error or block its Retry. Skip track moves focus immediately to the persistent Next control before replacing the failed track.

Options-save Retry keeps its focused action and pending feedback until that actual preference-only write settles, rejects repeated activation, and never restores, replaces or starts the saved queue. Failure retains Retry; success conditionally hands focus to Volume. Later navigation, option edits, overlays or window loss prevent a late handoff. Older preference or session-save receipts cannot clear a newer failed attempt. A later confirmed session save of the current options may resolve the warning with the same guarded focus behavior. Retain the failed-save warning until a matching save succeeds.

- Provide play, pause, previous, next, seeking, volume, shuffle, and repeat. Command-Left/Right invokes Previous/Next from ordinary page content, buttons and configuration tabs, preserving play/pause intent. Plain Left/Right arrows navigate configuration tabs. Space toggles playback from page content and retains native activation on focused controls. Editable fields, checkboxes, selects, sliders and menus keep their own key behavior; open dialogs and popovers suppress global playback shortcuts. Command-Up/Down adjusts volume only from non-interactive page content. Natural continuation after a DJ break follows the selected repeat mode, including repeating the same queue occurrence for repeat-one after completion, failure or Stop once the song has ended. Keep converted playback mode, shuffle history and pause intent; do not count a completion twice or replay heard news. Manual Next still skips the repeated song. Manual Next and Previous retain the current play/pause intent. Selecting another song while paused must not unexpectedly start playback; explicit Play actions start it.
- Show the current track, artist, artwork, playback position, and duration.
- Provide an expandable queue showing upcoming music.
- Keep playback running while the listener navigates and when the app is in the background.
- Support macOS media controls.

- Automatically restore the last queue, song, position, volume, shuffle and repeat after relaunch, paused and ready to play, without a resume prompt. Preserve queue order and the selected occurrence of duplicate songs. Keep volume, shuffle and repeat when the queue becomes empty, and persist changes to those controls with an empty queue. Startup must not save an empty placeholder over a pending or failed restoration; explicit Play or enqueue may replace it. Keep control changes made while startup data loads, including when queue restoration fails. Explain that the queue is still saved and offer explicit Retry. If player options cannot be saved, give them a separate retry that does not start music or retry queue restoration. Opening another account without starting or queueing music must not overwrite a saved session belonging to the previous account. Keep volume, shuffle and repeat separately for each Jellyfin server/account, including while its player is empty and another account owns the last saved queue. Returning to the queue owner restores its own options. Keep one last listening queue; explicit Play or enqueue may replace it.

- Handle unavailable tracks and interrupted connections without endless retries or silently losing the listening session. After the supported conversion attempt fails, keep a plain-language explanation with Retry and Skip track available. A late old load success or failure cannot replace a newer song or queue occurrence, change its playing/paused intent or show a stale error. Offline catalog errors retain the connection and offer Try again. Session expiry prefills server/username for sign-in and restores saved music paused. In the running app, same-account reauthentication preserves unsaved radio setup, edited scripts and manual preparation state through library selection, without saving or redispatch. Different account/server or explicit sign-out clears those unsaved drafts; quitting does not preserve them.
The exact recovery and queue persistence behavior must be verified with the connected server during implementation.
## Personal radio behavior

[The radio experience PRD](docs/RADIO_EXPERIENCE.md) defines the current listening, setup, preparation, review, and recovery contract. It supersedes the earlier manual-only station placeholder and planned-only workflow requirements. [News bucket workflows](docs/LISTENING_ROOM_WORKFLOW.md) describes service behavior and future extensions.
- Keep music browsing and playback as the default flow. AI setup is optional.

- Explicit sign-out pauses automatic preparation across all profiles before leaving the account. Retain saved enabled choices, setup, counters and history; require explicit Resume after sign-in. Close the generation gate immediately and cancel active manual/automatic text, speech and voice-preview work, including work waiting for keys or async review reads. No new provider dispatch may follow the sign-out boundary or an old callback after a quick new sign-in. Preserve completed recording publication and count it once. Persist the pause through restart and completed-run reconciliation. A delayed setup save or Resume cannot clear a newer sign-out pause. No automatic check starts on a signed-out launch. # Personal radio experience

Current product contract, 17 October 2026. This document and `REQUIREMENTS.md` replace earlier descriptions of a station placeholder, manual-only DJ tests, and a planned-only news runner. Implementation details and future extensions belong in `LISTENING_ROOM_WORKFLOW.md`.
## Who this is for

A listener has music in Jellyfin and wants to press Play, then hear occasional short news updates in a host's voice. They should not need to understand model prompts, request ledgers, or background jobs. A more involved listener can choose sources, interests, delivery, and schedules without operating a live broadcast desk.
The current radio uses the music queue the listener chooses. Mood describes the host's delivery. It does not analyze audio or choose music. News is prepared as complete recordings before playback.

## Everyday listening

The listener chooses songs, an album, a playlist, or a queue and presses Play. Browsing and setup do not interrupt music. Launching after quitting restores the prior listening context paused. News controls are optional and reachable from every library page.

Closing the macOS window with the red control or ⌘W hides it; the app keeps running. Music and already-authorized preparation continue. Activating the app brings back the same page, listening state, unsaved edits and pending or failed actions, restoring a minimized window when needed. Closing does not save changes or start or retry work. Use Pause, Cancel, or the preparation controls to stop their respective activities; Quit (⌘Q) ends the app and discards unsaved drafts.
Two independent choices govern radio behavior:
| Choice | Default | Effect | Does not imply |

| Automatically prepare news | Off | Check selected sources while the app process runs and Mac is awake; assess new articles; save qualifying script and voice audio | Playback, music selection, or running while the app has quit |
| DJ breaks | Off | Use saved matching fresh recordings at suitable song endings | Provider requests, enabling preparation, or speaking immediately |

Preparation defaults to every three hours, major developments only, maximum three automatic recordings per local day. Daily scheduled checks are also bounded by cadence. Text assessment can cost money without producing a recording. Limits apply to scheduled preparation for each profile, not an account-wide currency budget. Manual text/audio preparation and voice-preview generation are explicit additional provider actions outside those limits. Disclose that scope beside their controls; replaying cached audio makes no provider request. No source article is promised to be discovered.

Enabling or resuming preparation must use confirmed saved keys. If a required key was removed first, activation fails without changing the saved profile. If a key edit is requested during an enabled setup save, it waits until that save finishes. A later removal retains the saved preparation choice and setup explains what needs repair. Incomplete setup and OFF saves remain available without keys and do not wait for a pending key edit. X credentials are required only for selected X sources.

DJ breaks default to every three songs, counting natural completions rather than manual skips. A saved take may wait for a suitable ending. An empty ready list leaves music playing. Eligible recordings match the selected profile’s saved host, mood, interests and source selection, have a complete audio file and have not been heard or reserved elsewhere. At least one reference must establish freshness within the last 24 hours: use a valid publication date, or the preparation time when that reference has no usable date. A future-dated reference cannot satisfy freshness on its own. Over-music breaks that are too long for the current ending, or arrive too late, wait unheard for the next suitable song while music continues. A profile change releases a late old-profile claim rather than placing it on the new profile. Repeated interruptions and late endings must not replay old news or cause duplicate queue advances. Article identity ignores verified tracking fields while keeping original source links. A tracked and plain link to the same supported article must not cause another review or replay, including after restart. Semantic query fields remain part of the identity; saved review outcomes remain intact.

Music pause pauses speech and transition timing. Music pause does not pause the independent preparation workflow. Disabling DJ breaks stops its pending/active speech and keeps music available. Turn off automatic preparation is available during a running check. It immediately saves OFF for the named profile, prevents future checks, and requests cancellation without saving other setup edits. A failed stop remains visible after navigation and can be retried. A provider request already dispatched may have been charged. Saved results remain available.

A missing, empty, or incomplete audio file leaves its saved script, settings, and selected ID intact. Listen, use, and schedule are unavailable for that file. Explain how to load its script for an explicit replacement; never regenerate automatically. The normal Generate audio take action reuses a valid matching recording, including a later replacement. Generate another take explicitly requests a new variation. Manual completion names its original profile and says whether audio was saved or reused, with Review saved take. This result survives music navigation and profile switching until the next manual attempt. A different Jellyfin account/server or confirmed sign-out clears the unsaved completion notice while keeping saved recordings on this Mac. Review refreshes and focuses the exact recording without starting audio or changing selection. Unavailable recordings remain reviewable for their script and recovery guidance. Failed refresh or a missing result retains a retryable message. In the open manual tools, the result comes into view above the player without taking keyboard focus. Saved details show the original news interests and label missing publication dates.

Audition Pause keeps the recording and current position even when pressed during playback startup. Resume continues that recording; rapid pause/resume must not reset it or show a false error. Stop, leaving Saved audio, or starting music ends the audition. A genuine playback failure remains visible and allows an explicit new attempt. After restoring a missing or damaged file, Refresh followed by Listen or Schedule DJ break reopens the repaired recording without an app restart or provider request.

Seeking preserves a scheduled/active DJ break by default, following the global Keep the DJ when seeking setting. Seeking to the exact song endpoint follows repeat and queue order without counting a natural completion or advancing DJ cadence. Playback keeps its playing or paused intent. A retained break finishes before continuation; a paused break waits for Play. Seeking back into the song makes the retained break wait for its ending again. If the DJ has started speaking, pause the same clip at its current position, restore the music level, and resume only its remaining speech at the next suitable ending. Play after a paused rewind resumes music first. Already-finished speech is never replayed. The player explains when speech is waiting for the song ending. A seek short of the endpoint may still count when the remaining audio ends naturally. Explicit track replacement cancels its placement; an unheard automatic recording may wait for another ending. Transition settings control talkover or between-song delivery without regenerating voice audio. Preview transition in app Settings compares draft timings with sample music and a bundled saved voice. It needs no queue, key or provider request. The demo pauses music and leaves it paused when stopped or finished. Later music transport commands stop it, including paused song changes and seeks; volume, shuffle and repeat do not. Changing a draft timing/style or leaving General settings stops the demo without saving or starting it again. Canceled attempts cannot change a replacement preview or display stale errors.
## What the listener can see

The player popover shows playback state, selected playback profile, host, next song condition, upcoming/current script and source links, and last heard this session. A separate preparation line names the profile it describes and links to its setup. It must never describe the page's profile as the playback profile. A scheduled recording stays Upcoming until its transition starts and does not enter Last heard until speech actually plays. Last heard distinguishes On air, Paused, Played to the end and Interrupted; it is limited to this app session and remains visible when the playback profile changes. A failed saved-pool read shows Needs attention and Try again. Retrying shows Checking pool while it reads saved recordings and never prepares new text or voice.

News bucket shows the profile being inspected, preparation status, timestamp and reason for its last check, actual next check, daily check/recording usage, and fresh matching recordings ready to play. Count labels define their scope. Review history is global and says so. It initially shows 25 stories; Show more labels the next batch size. Keyboard expansion focuses the first newly revealed title, including the final batch, without opening its source. Tab continues through the new stories. Pointer expansion and passive updates leave focus alone. It is not a count of all news on the internet or money spent.

Automatic preparation and manual activity have separate status. If activity or saved news cannot be checked, retain the draft, lock setup/profile changes and offer Retry. Independently confirmed automatic settings and scheduled counters remain useful; cached recordings say last loaded. If automatic status itself cannot be refreshed, show only the last saved automatic setting, with no current-looking counters or last-run claim. The player’s automatic preparation line follows the same saved-status rule. A successful status retry restores editing without saving the draft or starting generation.
Use these states in ordinary language:
| State | What the user sees or can do |

| Partial source coverage | Keep usable stories and show the saved named source warning beside ready, draft and scheduled/current stories, and in the player’s DJ story view. Label missing or invalid reference dates Date unavailable, including in article history. If source reads fail or return unreadable data and no fresh story can be assessed, report incomplete coverage as a failure and require Resume. If readable stories were assessed but none was selected while coverage was incomplete, record Incomplete source coverage, keep preparation enabled and wait for the next scheduled check. Make no recording and do not retry immediately. Complete readable coverage with no qualifying story remains a no-news result. For Hacker News, a missing or mismatched story identity, unreadable recent story or unsafe supplied link counts as incomplete coverage. Deleted, dead, known non-story and validly dated old/future items are normal exclusions. A story without a URL may use its verified discussion link. For X searches, accept an explicit empty post list or an omitted list with a zero result count as empty. Unreadable post data, malformed error results and contradictory supplied counts require a coverage warning; usable posts remain available. Undated entries are skipped in automatic checks with an explanation. |
| Setup incomplete | Identify missing sources, host, mood, or provider keys and offer the relevant setup action |
| Off | Preparation is off; saved audio is available |
| Checking | A persisted check is in progress; do not claim audio is ready |
| Recording saved | Show finish time; it becomes eligible only if it matches current setup and freshness rules |
| No qualifying story | Show actual reason; no speech is generated; music continues |

| Incomplete source coverage after assessment | Name the unreadable sources, say no story was selected from the readable sources and show the next scheduled check; preparation stays on, no recording is made and no immediate paid retry occurs |
| Daily limit | Say which daily count reached its cap and when checks can resume; this is not an error |
| Paused after failure | Show saved error and Resume preparation; missing or rejected keys direct Settings → Provider keys, independently of saved DJ playback; avoid automatic paid retries |
| Interrupted | Explain that completion is uncertain; reconcile saved artifacts and require explicit resume if unresolved |
| Room unavailable | Explain that preparation and automatic playback require an available room |
| Status refresh failed | Keep last-known data with an unavailable/stale notice and Retry; do not report a false Off state |

A due timestamp is a target, not a promise. A running manual operation can delay preparation. Sleep or quit prevents execution. On return, coalesce missed slots into one current check. Do not read yesterday's backlog as today's news.

## Done criteria and evidence

Current acceptance, as requested by Anton on 16 October 2026, starts at 1280×720 and normal 100% app zoom. Smaller windows and enlarged zoom, including 200%, are deferred for later. Keep their existing behavior and historical evidence, but do not repeat or expand those checks during this goal. This supersedes the older size/zoom acceptance cases.

Use the [observable acceptance checklist](ACCEPTANCE_CHECKLIST.md) to trace each STAR result to concrete checks. Every linked result remains required; a grouped fixture or passing build cannot substitute for the complete story.
Disabled controls and pending forms keep readable labels and values; a disabled primary action uses a neutral surface rather than faded text. Active transition-stage timings remain readable.

A feature is complete when its current contract is consistent across PRD, service behavior, and UI; affected scenarios pass focused end-to-end or manual checks; and failures/limits can be understood from visible text without opening implementation files. Review actual artifacts, not only proposals. Reopen a decision when a failing scenario exposes a gap.

Engineering verification uses local Electron or an isolated renderer/service fixture with real storage paths and substituted providers. Fixture results do not establish source coverage, actual provider delivery, or subjective voice/transition quality. Record exact checks and remaining limitations in `IMPLEMENTATION.md` and the requirement-by-requirement [acceptance audit](UX_ACCEPTANCE.md). Do not claim the 90% acceptance milestone until the denominator and current evidence are recorded there. Do not equate internal review with regular-user validation or call the UX perfect without evidence from listeners.
Weather, calendar/reminders, budget pricing estimates, AI song selection, external station broadcasting, and release packaging are outside this contract. They should not appear as working controls.

Shared source deletion names every setup profile using that source before confirmation. If the selected playback profile loses its last source, confirmation explains that DJ breaks will turn off and points to News bucket to choose another source. Cancel preserves the source; confirmed deletion removes its references from those profiles. Saved recordings keep their original source provenance. Saving sources never prepares a story by itself.

## Observed listener acceptance

The [listener session protocol](LISTENER_ACCEPTANCE.md) checks music-first discovery, optional setup, the two opt-ins and costs, named profile activity, independent stops, saved-news listening and sign-out without coaching. Use a separate pilot before the planned five-listener validation cohort. Ten first-attempt tasks per listener give 50 observations; at least 45 must succeed unaided, and every critical invariant and cost/opt-in comprehension check must pass. A passing cohort score describes those observed sessions. It does not substitute for live source/provider, VoiceOver, device or full requirement acceptance. No listener result is claimed yet.
